issues.detail: Error handling is thin: there are no steps for a failed checksum, a server that fails to start or a port already in use, or a failed fetch, and Example 2 backgrounds the server with '&' but only says to stop it by PID without showing how.

scenarios.name: markdown-dump-for-llm-prompt
scenarios.rationale: B gives the exact `lightpanda fetch` command with `--dump markdown`, `--dump-selector "main"`, `--strip-mode clutter`, `--dump-max-bytes 40000` and redirects to a file, while A uses `fetch --dump markdown` and a file redirect but wrongly claims there is no size flag, uses awk truncation, uses underscore flag names, and says main-content narrowing is not possible.

scenarios.name: puppeteer-link-scraper-over-cdp
scenarios.rationale: Both meet the rubric (loopback bind on 9222, no-auth note, puppeteer-core, connect with browserWSEndpoint, context, page.evaluate over anchors, close page/context/disconnect); A sits slightly higher because it explicitly says the endpoint has no authentication and gives richer link output, while B also covers PID handling and stopping the server but only collects raw hrefs and uses a `--obey-robots` flag spelling that may be wrong.
